# HomuraJS

> Time Travel State & Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) History Engine for JavaScript ("Git for Application State")

Author & Maintainer: Biagio Scaglia — https://github.com/biagio-scaglia
Repository: https://github.com/biagio-scaglia/homura-js
Documentation: https://biagio-scaglia.github.io/homura-js/
Full AI Knowledge Base: https://biagio-scaglia.github.io/homura-js/llms-full.txt
npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@biagioscaglia/homurajs
License: MIT

## Overview

HomuraJS is an open-source state management and time-travel history engine that replaces conventional 1D linear undo/redo stacks with a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG). When a user steps back in history and makes a new modification, HomuraJS preserves all timeline branches instead of permanently destroying future states.

Key capabilities:
- **Non-Destructive DAG Branching**: Fork alternative timelines, navigate historical states, and reconcile branches via 3-way merge.
- **Copy-On-Write Proxy Immutability**: Mutate states directly in draft proxies with structural memory sharing.
- **Deep Structural Diffing**: Calculate exact recursive dot-path differences between any two states in the DAG.
- **Zero-JS Static Forms & WordPress Crash Recovery**: Auto-bind HTML and WordPress forms to browser storage (LocalStorage/SessionStorage) with zero configuration.
- **Embedded Diagnostic DevTools**: Standalone GUI with interactive timeline graph, JSON state inspector, and step scrubber.
- **Zero Dependencies**: Core engine weighs < 5.2 kB gzip.

## Monorepo Packages

- `@biagioscaglia/homurajs`: Unified meta-package bundle + standalone browser CDN (`dist/index.global.js`).
- `@homura-js/core`: Core DAG graph engine, Proxy draft immutability, structural diffing, snapshot registry, persistence, and middleware.
- `@homura-js/devtools`: Embedded diagnostic UI with visual timeline tree, JSON state inspector, diff viewer, and playback controls.
- `@homura-js/vanilla`: Frameworkless reactive DOM bindings (`bindState`) and Zero-JS form auto-recovery engine (`bindForm`, `data-homura-form`).
- `@homura-js/react`: React 18+ hook (`useHomura`) powered by `useSyncExternalStore` with selector optimization.
- `@homura-js/vue`: Vue 3 Composition API hook (`useHomura`) and plugin.
- `@homura-js/db`: Versioned embedded database state (SQLite/In-Memory) & Full-Stack forensic correlation between client UI states (#184), network traces, and DB transactions (#52).

## WordPress & WooCommerce Integration

HomuraJS provides an official WordPress plugin (`homura-time-travel-form-recovery`) for form crash recovery and time-travel:
- **Shortcodes**: `[homura_form]`, `[homura_undo]`, `[homura_redo]`, `[homura_status]`, `[homura_breadcrumbs]`.
- **Auto-Hooks**: Automatically detects and protects WooCommerce Checkout (`.woocommerce-checkout`), Contact Form 7 (`.wpcf7 form`), WPForms (`.wpforms-form`), Gravity Forms (`.gform_wrapper`), and Elementor Forms (`.elementor-form`).
- **Client-Side Privacy**: 100% client-side storage (LocalStorage). No external servers or tracking.

## Zero-JS Static Site Form Usage

```html
<!-- Load HomuraJS from CDN -->
<script src="https://unpkg.com/@biagioscaglia/homurajs/dist/index.global.js"></script>

<!-- Auto-bound form with crash recovery and undo/redo -->
<form data-homura-form="lead_quote" data-homura-persist="localstorage">
  <span data-homura-status></span>
  <input type="text" name="name" placeholder="Name" />
  <input type="email" name="email" placeholder="Email" />
  <button type="button" data-homura-undo>Undo</button>
  <button type="button" data-homura-redo>Redo</button>
</form>
```

## TypeScript Quick Start

```ts
import { createHomura } from '@biagioscaglia/homurajs';

const homura = createHomura({
  initialState: { counter: 0, user: { name: 'Homura', role: 'Architect' } }
});

// Mutate via Copy-On-Write draft proxy
homura.update(draft => {
  draft.counter += 10;
  draft.user.role = 'Lead';
}, { label: 'Increment and promote' });

// Time-travel navigation
homura.undo(); // State reverts to counter: 0
homura.redo(); // State returns to counter: 10

// Branching
homura.createBranch('experimental');
homura.update(draft => { draft.counter = 999; });
```
